references.text: Jacob's prophetic words over Simeon and Levi refer directly to their violent act in Shechem: 'Their swords are instruments of violence... Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce.'
Simeon and Levi's deception with the circumcision proposal laid the groundwork for the attack on the third day, when the men of Shechem were in great pain after being circumcised.
The Mosaic law's instruction to strike the inhabitants of an idolatrous city with the edge of the sword has thematic similarity to Simeon and Levi's action, but here it is a divine command.
The Israelites remained in camp until they were healed from circumcision, illustrating the pain the men of Shechem experienced when Simeon and Levi attacked them on the third day.
Jesus' warning that those who take up the sword will perish by the sword reflects the consequences of violent vengeance seen in Simeon and Levi's action at Shechem.
Jacob's reaction to Simeon and Levi's act—he feared revenge from neighboring peoples—but his sons defended themselves: 'Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?'
Direct allusion and fulfillment of prophecy; Jacob's judgment in 49:5 is the theological interpretation of the event in 34:25.
